description: Opens the Godot editor on a project, or restarts the one already connected. open refuses while an editor of the project is already running and has not reached this server, naming its pid, rather than putting a second on the project. The editor is an ordinary visible one on the desktop in use, and on Windows it is shown without being activated, so opening or reopening it does not take the keyboard from whatever the user is typing in. hidden: true opens it headless instead and, on Windows, on a desktop of its own, where the games it plays go too; a hidden editor serves the bridge, the language server and the debug adapter as a visible one does. A game a visible editor plays opens as a window on the desktop in use. An editor goes on serving the addon it read at startup, so restart is what puts a gdharness upgrade into effect, and nothing else here restarts one; it saves open scenes on the way out and answers with the version that came back. An editor a server opened is started again by the server, visible unless hidden: true is passed again, once the old one has gone: it waits 90 seconds for that, or GDHARNESS_EDITOR_RESTART_TIMEOUT_MS, and an old editor still running after it is not replaced, since the new one would find its ports held. One opened by hand restarts itself, which only one with a window can do, because the engine hands back none of the arguments it was started with. editor_status says which editor is connected and whether it is holding an old addon. Opening a project is a save and so is closing one, which is the part that is not obvious from outside: the editor imports the project on open and writes project.godot back, and Godot writes only what differs from its own defaults, so a key named deliberately at its default value is dropped either way. A restart says which under settingsDropped in its own answer because it waits for the editor to return. An open cannot, since it answers as soon as the process exists and the save happens during the import minutes later, so editor_status carries that reading once the editor has connected. Nothing else will say a key went until something depends on one. A restart of an editor this server opened is a quit and then a launch, and this server can be ended between them, usually by the reconnect the restart was being taken for: the editor is gone and nothing replaces it. That is written down before the quit, so the next server says so under restartInterrupted in editor_status rather than waiting for an editor that is not coming, and open finishes it, saying so under finishesRestart. An open is refused when the editor it would start could never reach this server: a project other than the one this server serves, whose editor dials that project's own server; a project without the gdharness editor addon installed and enabled; and a project whose editor a restart is already bringing back. Operations: open (needs projectPath): open the editor on a project; restart: restart the connected editor and wait for it. Default open.

hidden.description: Open the editor headless and, on Windows, on a desktop of its own, so no window of it or of the games it plays appears. Default false: one visible editor, shown without taking the focus. On restart only for an editor a server opened; one opened by hand comes back as it was, so hidden is refused there.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.

name: editor_launch
